..
Issued at 1242 PM CDT Sat Sep 19 2026

A broad surface trough extends from northeast Iowa, southwest
across Kansas and into the Texas and Oklahoma Panhandles. A 
convectively- reinforced outflow/gravity wave associated with 
widespread morning convection had pushed well south through 
central Illinois but should start to slowly return northward as 
the aforementioned trough begins advancing towards the 
Mississippi river through the rest of the afternoon. This 
boundary may make it back as far north as about a Cedar Rapids 
to Ottawa to Rensselaer line through late this afternoon with 
temperatures recovering back into the lower 80s and dewpoints 
into the lower 70s. 

To the north of this returning (and eventually stalling)
boundary, isentropic upglide will increase significantly late 
this afternoon and evening as strengthening 925-700 mb southwest
to westerly flow rides up and over the sloping frontal zone as 
a positively-tilted shortwave shifts out of central Iowa. As 
this occurs, a remnant dry layer from 925-700 mb--leftover from 
morning convection--will saturate, leading to the redevelopment 
of showers and thunderstorms.

Trends in high-resolution guidance have generally been towards a 
slower progression to things, with redevelopment not occurring 
meaningfully until after about 7-8 PM or so. That said, given 
the magnitude of forecast isentropic upglide developing late 
this afternoon, would not be surprised if more vigorous 
convective development still occurs during the late afternoon 
and early evening. Regardless, the environment in place will be 
supportive of torrential rain-producing thunderstorms tonight, 
with PWATs well into record territory, quasi-persistent upper 
jet divergence, and a modest (yet sufficient) 25-30 kt 
southwesterly low-level jet impinging on the aforementioned 
stationary frontal zone. Generally easterly/east-southeasterly 
cloud bearing flow, aligned more-or-less parallel to the 
initiating boundaries, will result in a potential for training 
convective elements. Latest guidance suggests the main potential
heavy rain corridor may essentially overlap with the location 
of this morning's widespread steady rainfall which has started 
to saturate soils. Have extended the previous Flood Watch 
through early Sunday morning. Did contemplate adding a few zones
on the south end of the watch, but at this time it looks like 
activity that does push farther southward may end up being 
somewhat more progressive, limiting overall residence time. 
Can't rule out the need for an expansion at some point, but the  
widespread heavy rain threat appears too low to warrant that at 
this time. 

The main synoptic cold front will push south across the region
on Sunday morning. Fairly widespread showers and embedded 
storms may be ongoing after daybreak, but expecting the bulk of 
activity to gradually shift southward through the morning and 
afternoon. A trailing shortwave may result in a bit of a flare 
up of shower activity towards midday/early afternoon, but the 
main MUCAPE axis will steadily be shifting southward during this
time. Lingering saturation up through about 10 kft and modest 
ascent may result in areas of showers or even steady drizzle 
continuing north of the frontal zone into the afternoon (north 
of I-80), but we should eventually start to scour out the low 
cloud deck sufficiently to bring most of the lingering precip 
chances to an end late in the day. 

An additional series of disturbances are slated to rotate atop
the frontal zone Sunday night through Tuesday as 
broad/persistent cyclonic flow develops across the region. 
Forecast soundings suggest we may be dealing with at least 
periods of showers and drizzle from Sunday night through the 
better part of Tuesday evening before a drier low-level airmass 
pushes in from the east. Persistent cloud cover and east to 
northeasterly winds will keep temperatures seasonably cool in 
the 60s. 

High pressure is forecast to build more meaningfully across the 
region on Wednesday and Thursday, but another disturbance may
clip our area towards the end of the week.

Carlaw
